clue.text: No movement here with record to preserve

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: A place where nothing moves, with an archive of records to be kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam of logs in a river is a blockage where nothing can move, hence any deadlock.

clue.text: Start shooting to increase global warning?

definitions.meaning: 'warning' plays on the warning shots of the first sense

explanation.surface: Firing a few shots as a way to put the whole world on alert.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin firing is the military command phrase; an unenclosed hearth fire burns fuel, worsening climate heating.

clue.text: Disposal in spirit following setter in French city

indicators.note: following places the spirit-and-sale part after the French 'I'

parts.note: the setter says 'I', which in French is je

indicators.note: in puts the disposal word inside the spirit word

parts.note: rum is a spirit
a sale disposes of goods

explanation.surface: Getting rid of something in liquor, after the compiler has gone to a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' tempts as a definition, but 'French' belongs with 'setter' (JE) and the city is the Holy City; this is also the hymn on which the puzzle's theme turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy city in Israel is the subject of Blake's poem set as a famous hymn.

clue.text: French lady's psyche seriously disturbed?

parts.note: mad means seriously disturbed in mind
ame (âme) is the French word for the soul or psyche, the question mark and the French theme allowing it

explanation.surface: Is the mind of a Frenchwoman deeply unbalanced?
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' is the definition's word, but the clue's question mark licenses taking psyche in French as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a married woman serves as a word for a French lady.

clue.text: Tree, by squeezing it, produces vitriol

parts.note: acer is the maple genus, a tree

indicators.note: squeezing means the word by closes round the word it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree squeezed hard yields a corrosive acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol in its figurative sense is bitter, caustic speech, which is sharpness of temper.

clue.text: See 6
Afflicted gannet's prangs, laden repeatedly at end of 3

indicators.note: afflicted suggests something knocked about and damaged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written with its S
taken as written
the word laden given again and again, three times in all

explanation.surface: A suffering seabird crashes over and over, weighed down, at the close of the poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes GANNETS and PRANGS with LADEN three times; '3' is the Jerusalem hymn, whose last line ends with these words.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake's lyric closes 'In England's green and pleasant land', so this phrase stands at the end of that hymn.

clue.text: 3's creator born 23, perhaps

parts.note: 23 is Geneva, an example of a lake

explanation.surface: The hymn's author was born in Geneva, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: William Blake wrote the poem known as Jerusalem, so he is that work's creator.

clue.text: Quitter's broken funny bone

indicators.note: broken means the letters of quitter are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: the 's is 'is', a link; quitter alone is the fodder
rum means funny in the sense of odd

explanation.surface: Someone who gives up has broken their funny bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the elbow's funny bone, but 'funny' is RUM and the bone is a small wrist bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The triquetrum is one of the eight carpal bones of the wrist.

clue.text: Reduced from A to D, say — D, say, caused dread

definitions.text: Reduced from A to D, say

parts.note: taken as written
eg (for example) means say

indicators.note: caused works the letters of dread into a new shape, the result the anagram produces

explanation.surface: Being marked down from top grade to a D brings fear.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator 'caused' rearranges DREAD into RADED; the second 'D, say' is wordplay, separate from the D in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being demoted down a scale, as from grade A to grade D, is being lowered in rank.

clue.text: Fields for grazing partly by French company

indicators.note: partly means only the opening part of the word grazing is used

parts.note: Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company

explanation.surface: Pastures for grazing beside a French firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fields' looks like meadows but is the surname of Gracie Fields, the much-loved English singer and comic actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Gracie Fields was a famous British entertainer, so her surname clues her first name.

clue.text: Coincidental stimulus externally applied to a funny one

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd and twisted, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chance prompt applied from outside to an amusing person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges STIMULUS, A and ONE together; 'externally applied to' is surface padding joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that coincide happen at the same moment, which is the meaning of simultaneous.

clue.text: A disturbance in spirit for 7 in 3 with 22?

indicators.note: in puts the a-plus-disturbance part inside the spirit word

parts.note: cheer means good spirits
taken as written
a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: Trouble breaking out in high spirits, for the poet in his hymn with fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake (7) in Jerusalem (3) asks 'Bring me my chariot of fire' (22), so he is a charioteer.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet calls for a chariot of fire in the hymn, so he would drive it as its charioteer.

clue.text: Sound of stream at seaside resort

indicators.note: sound of means the word for stream is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Hearing a brook at a coastal holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: RHYL is a seaside resort on the North Wales coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyl is a holiday town on the coast of North Wales, a seaside resort.

clue.text: Step down and subside, holding investigators back

indicators.note: holding means the subside word wraps round the other part

parts.note: abate means subside

indicators.note: back means the investigators' abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Resign and calm down while keeping the detectives at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CID to DIC. CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is Britain's plain-clothes police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or office, to resign from it.

clue.text: Sort of thinking starting with thinking more or less well?

definitions.text: Sort of thinking starting with thinking

parts.note: c (circa) means about, more or less
an artesian well is one where water rises under its own pressure

explanation.surface: A kind of thought that begins with thinking, roughly well?
explanation.walkthrough: Descartes' philosophy famously starts from 'I think, therefore I am', thinking as its starting point.
explanation.definitionFit: Descartes built his system on the certainty of his own thought, so his method of reasoning bears his adjective.

clue.text: The self-contained universe, by and large

definitions.meaning: everything contained within everything, a whole holding itself
taken all round, on the whole

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everything considered, on balance; read literally it is everything inside everything.

clue.text: Second city (American one's about first) to grow pineapple

parts.note: b is second, as in a B grade or the second letter
Rome is a city

indicators.note: about means the American city wraps round the other letter

parts.note: one being a city, LA (Los Angeles) is an American city
I is the Roman numeral one, hence first

explanation.surface: Another city, an American one going round first, to farm pineapples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' in 'American one' means a city, so it is LA, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Bromelia is the genus that gives the pineapple family its name, plants like the pineapple.

clue.text: Put to flight revellers in un-English way

indicators.note: un-English means the abbreviation for English is removed

parts.note: a route is a way

explanation.surface: Drive off partygoers in a manner not at all English.
explanation.walkthrough: A rout is both a crushing defeat that sends troops fleeing and, in old usage, a noisy band of revellers; ROUTE without E gives it a third time.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an enemy is to defeat it so it flees; an old sense of the noun is a rowdy gathering.

clue.text: Last on stalk to produce affection

parts.note: end means the last part
an ear of corn grows on a stalk

explanation.surface: The final grain on a stem gives rise to fondness.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone feel fondness, to cause affection.

clue.text: Novel loner … raced with stunning results

definitions.text: Novel loner … raced with stunning results

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something fresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solitary figure in a book ran with spectacular outcomes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the borstal boy in Alan Sillitoe's 'The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Runner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sillitoe's story follows a solitary young athlete who races cross-country, the title loner.

explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' and 'lake' sound like one watery scene, but 'Sort of pool' is GENE.

clue.text: Colourless Arthurian site setter's object too old, I might say

indicators.note: colourless means the word for colour, tint, is taken away

parts.note: Tintagel in Cornwall is linked with King Arthur's birth
the setter's is 'I'm', I am
it is an object pronoun, a thing

explanation.surface: A drab legendary castle the compiler finds too ancient to like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourless' removes TINT from TINTAGEL, leaving AGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An age limit is a cutoff at which someone is told they are too old, as an official might say.

clue.text: Lined with ice for Zeppelin

parts.note: a rink is a sheet of ice
Led is the word before Zeppelin in the rock band's name

explanation.surface: Coated in ice, as an airship might be.
explanation.walkthrough: Led Zeppelin is the British rock band; LED is the part that goes with 'Zeppelin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that is lined has creases, which is what wrinkled means.
